notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 25 this time, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

I tried to open the verse-by-verse commentaries you listed: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. The research tool hit its usage limit on the first attempt and refused every call after that, so nothing came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Without any pages, I'd be writing from memory and couldn't give real URLs, so I've left the notes out rather than make them up.

**What I'll do when the tool is working again:**
1. **The usual reading of each verse:** Enduring Word, plus Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary and others on biblehub.com and studylight.org, and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant groups disagree:** I'll search each group's own sites for the verses most likely to divide them. These are the "feast for all peoples" (v. 6) and "swallow up death forever" (vv. 7–8). Verse 8 is quoted in 1 Corinthians 15:54 and echoed in Revelation 21:4.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, debate over which city v. 2 means and how to read the Moab passage in vv. 10–12). For Catholic and Orthodox readings, newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org (for example, whether the v. 6 banquet points to the Lord's Supper). I'll include popular modern teaching only if these sites discuss it.

If you send the request again, I'll start with those sources and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after every point.
